title: FCOS3D: Fully Convolutional One-Stage Monocular 3D Object Detection
venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision Workshops (ICCVW)

problem.summary: It is much more challenging than conventional 2D cases due to its inherent ill-posed property, which is mainly reflected in the lack of depth information. Recent progress on 2D detection offers opportunities to better solving this problem.
statements: It is much more challenging than conventional 2D cases due to its inherent ill-posed property, which is mainly reflected in the lack of depth information.
Recent progress on 2D detection offers opportunities to better solving this problem.
However, it is non-trivial to make a general adapted 2D detector work in this 3D task.
In this paper, we study this problem with a practice built on a fully convolutional single-stage detector and propose a general framework FCOS3D.

solution.summary: In this paper, we study this problem with a practice built on a fully convolutional single-stage detector and propose a general framework FCOS3D. In this paper, we adopt a simple yet efficient method to enable a 2D detector to predict 3D localization.
solution.approach: In this paper, we study this problem with a practice built on a fully convolutional single-stage detector and propose a general framework FCOS3D.

evidence.quote: In this paper, we study this problem with a practice built on a fully convolutional single-stage detector and propose a general framework FCOS3D.
In this paper, we adopt a simple yet efficient method to enable a 2D detector to predict 3D localization.
As a practical implementation, we build our method on FCOS [31], a simple anchor-free fully convolutional singlestage detector.

experiments.summary: Our solution achieves 1st place out of all the vision-only methods in the nuScenes 3D detection challenge of NeurIPS 2020. It achieves a good trade-off between accuracy and efficiency in our experiments.

deploymentClaims: Abstract Monocular 3D object detection is an important task for autonomous driving considering its advantage of low cost.
Various models such as Faster R-CNN [27], RetinaNet [18], and FCOS [31] significantly promote the progress of the field and benefit various applications like autonomous driving.
So monocular 3D object detection, as a simple and cheap setting for deployment, becomes a much meaningful research problem nowadays.
